title: Findings (CLI output, and the input to adjudication)
description:
Result of a scan. Every entry is a candidate raised by a detector, not a conclusion: nothing in this document asserts that anything is unlawful.

COMPATIBILITY, AND ONE RECORDED BREAK. This schema carries no version of its own — `bundle.version` is the rule bundle's, not this file's — so a consumer pins it by pinning the repository. It is not compatible in either direction across every change, and the breaks are recorded here rather than discovered: (1) 2026-08-27, `suppressed_by_corroboration[]` gained two REQUIRED properties, `cause` and `lines`. Neither direction is a malformed document: it is this file that moved. A pinned older consumer must either keep validating old documents with the old schema and new documents with this one, or stop validating and read the two new properties as optional. (2) 2026-08-28, two OPTIONAL top-level keys were added, `dependency_inventory` and `declared_vendors_without_candidates`, and later the same day one OPTIONAL counter, `stats.manifests_not_usable`, which breaks in the same one direction for the same reason (`stats` also sets `additionalProperties: false`). THE BREAK WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN AVOIDED, and the alternative is named so the choice is auditable: relaxing the top-level `additionalProperties` to true would make every future key invisible to validation, including a misspelled one, which is a larger and permanent loss than a one-directional break a pinned consumer fixes by pinning this schema too. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHAT FIRES: measured over the eight pinned pass-1 trees, the `candidates` array is byte-for-byte identical before and after, and so are the finding_ids, the locations and the SARIF output. THIS BREAK RUNS BOTH WAYS, which (2) did not, and that is why it is recorded separately rather than folded into it. Forwards: a document written on or after this change is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it, because the `declared` item sets additionalProperties: false — the same mechanism as (2), one `must NOT have additional properties` per declaration. Backwards: a document written EARLIER ON 2026-08-28, in the few hours when the inventory existed without `field`, is INVALID against this schema, because `field` is required — one `must have required property 'field'` per declaration. Both directions measured with ajv (2020-12) on 2026-08-28. REQUIRED RATHER THAN OPTIONAL, and the alternative is named so the choice is auditable: an optional `field` would let a producer that stopped labelling declarations validate silently, and a consumer could not tell a runtime declaration from a build-time one it was never told about — the same reason `declared_only` is written on every entry rather than only where it is true. The narrow window in which unlabelled documents were written is a cheaper loss than a label a producer may drop. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHAT FIRES EITHER: the widening adds `declared` entries and one label, and the `candidates` array is untouched by it. (4) 2026-09-16, the per-file wall-clock budget: files_not_read[].reason gained the value time-budget with the optional budget_ms and elapsed_ms beside it, files_partially_read[] gained the optional stopped_for_time block, stats gained the optional files_stopped_for_time, and files_partially_read[] RELAXED its required list from file+threshold+lines to file alone. THE POPULATION OF AFFECTED DOCUMENTS IS EXACTLY THE SCANS IN WHICH A FILE EXCEEDED ITS BUDGET, which is the whole point of the design: a scan where no file did writes the document it wrote before the budget existed, byte for byte, and the three corpus repositories were re-scanned and compared to their pre-budget hashes to hold that. Forwards, for a document that DOES carry one of the new fields: it is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before this date - a reason enum value that copy does not list, and additionalProperties false on the item objects and on stats. Backwards: every document written before this date is still valid here, including under the relaxed required list, because relaxing required can only admit documents. THE RELAXATION WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN AVOIDED and the alternative is named so the choice is auditable: keeping threshold and lines required would have made a time-stopped row write threshold for a ceiling that took nothing and lines as an empty array, which states a measurement nobody took and contradicts the sentence on lines itself; a conditional requirement needs a combinator this schema states nowhere and that findings-schema-check.mjs asserts the absence of. The consumer-visible cost is that row.lines.length must become row.lines?.length ?? 0, and the two consumers in this repository (read-scope.ts, test-rules.ts) were changed with it. It breaks in the same ONE direction and for the same reason (2) does, and the asymmetry is again the whole reason it is a smaller event than (1): a document written BEFORE this date is still valid here, because the key is not required; a document written on or after it and carrying the key is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it, because the TOP LEVEL sets additionalProperties: false - one must NOT have additional properties. THE BREAK WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN AVOIDED, and the alternative is named so the choice is auditable: writing the index into an existing container (stats, or coverage_limits) would put a list of files behind a name that means something else, and relaxing the top-level additionalProperties to true would make every future key invisible to validation, which (2) already refused for the same reason. WHAT IS NEW HERE AND IS NOT IN (1) TO (4): this run writes FILES THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT DESCRIBE, holding verbatim source code from the scanned tree, under the directory --out names. This document still holds no excerpt. See context_payloads' own description, and product/packages/cli/src/context.ts. It breaks in the same ONE direction as (2) and (5) and for the same mechanism, one level down: a document written BEFORE this date is still valid here, because the key is not required; a document written on or after it and carrying the key is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it, because context_payloads sets additionalProperties: false - one must NOT have additional properties. THE POPULATION OF AFFECTED DOCUMENTS IS EXACTLY THE SCANS THAT WROTE PAYLOAD FILES, which is the same population (5) named, and a scan run with --context-window 0 or PRODUCT_CLI_CONTEXT=0 writes neither the index nor this key. THE BREAK WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN AVOIDED, and the alternative is named so the choice is auditable: a top-level cost_preview beside context_payloads would put a figure derived entirely from payloads[] outside the object that carries them, and a reader holding a document with no payload index would find a launch count with no launches under it. (7) 2026-09-23, TEN PROPERTIES WERE REMOVED, each a line of the scanned tree copied into this document: `suppressed_by_corroboration[].line_text`, `suppressed_by_corroboration[].lines[].line_text`, `candidates[].locations[].resolved_from[].definition_text`, `candidates[].locations[].corroborated_from.line_text`, `candidates[].locations[].corroborated_in_project_from.line_text`, `applicability[].limbs[].supporting[].line_text`, `applicability[].limbs[].opposing[].line_text`, `applicability[].contradictions[].evidence[].line_text`, `suppressed_by_guard[].lineText` and `suppressed_by_guard[].guardLineText`. Every line is still NAMED - `file` with `line`, `definition_line`, `guardFile` with `guardLine` - and a reader opens it in their own tree. It breaks in BOTH directions, like (1) and by the mirror image of its mechanism: every object that lost a property sets additionalProperties: false, so a document written before this date that carries any of these records is INVALID here (must NOT have additional properties), and a document written on or after it is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it, where each of the ten was required (must have required property). THE BREAK WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN AVOIDED: leaving the properties optional would let a freshly written document carry the text again and still validate, which is the state this change exists to end. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHAT FIRES: on three measured repositories the new document equals the old one with exactly these properties deleted, modulo the four run-identity fields the pins already ignore and, on the largest tree only, the `bytes` and `sha256` of the one `context_payloads.payloads[]` row whose payload file copied a candidate carrying one of them (that file equals the old one with the same property deleted); the other 90 payload files and the orientation files are byte-identical. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REMOVE: `candidates[].locations[].matched_token` and `candidates[].kinds.groups[].matched_token` are folded text taken from the matched clauses, and `applicability[]` evidence `value` is the collector's capture from the line; neither is a whole line, and both are decided separately. (8) 2026-10-20, the structural reading's time allowance: files_partially_read[] gained the OPTIONAL structural_reading_stopped block. It breaks in the same ONE direction as (2) and for the same mechanism: a document written before this date is still valid here, because the block is not required; a document carrying it is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it, because the item sets additionalProperties: false. THE POPULATION OF AFFECTED DOCUMENTS IS EXACTLY THE SCANS IN WHICH A FILE'S STRUCTURAL READING PASSED ITS ALLOWANCE; a scan where none did writes the document it wrote before. NOTHING HERE REMOVES A CANDIDATE THE LINE READING RAISES: the file is still read by every rule, line by line. (9) 2026-10-22, what stood at a path: excluded_by_walker[].reason gained six values, named-pipe, socket, device, link-to-folder, link-to-nothing and could-not-open, and the not-readable-as-code member of coverage_limits gained the count entries_not_regular_or_not_opened, written only where it is not zero. It breaks in the same ONE direction as (4) and for the same mechanism: a document written before this date is still valid here; a document carrying one of the new values is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it, which does not list the value. THE POPULATION OF AFFECTED DOCUMENTS IS EXACTLY THE SCANS OF A TREE THAT HOLDS SUCH AN ENTRY: a named pipe, a socket or a device (which a clone cannot carry, and a folder copied or unpacked whole can), a symbolic link to a folder (until this date refused as binary-content), a symbolic link that leads nowhere (until this date dropped without a word), or an entry the walker could not open (until this date refused as binary-content, or dropped). A scan of any other tree writes the document it wrote before. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHAT FIRES: no such entry was ever read by a rule. (10) 2026-10-24, a link out of the scanned folder: excluded_by_walker[].reason gained one value, link-to-outside, a symbolic link to a file outside the scanned folder, which is never read; it is counted and named with the others in the not-readable-as-code member. It breaks in the same ONE direction as (4) and (9): a document written before this date is still valid here; a document carrying the new value is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it. THE POPULATION OF AFFECTED DOCUMENTS IS EXACTLY THE SCANS OF A TREE THAT HOLDS A SYMBOLIC LINK TO A FILE OUTSIDE IT (a clone can carry one). Until this date such a link was read as a file of the tree, and what fired on its lines fired; it no longer is, so those candidates are gone, and a scan of any other tree writes the document it wrote before. (11) 2026-11-01, the walker's own bounds: excluded_by_walker[].reason gained three values, link-not-followed, a symbolic link whose chain the walker did not resolve because doing so would pass the work it allows for one link or for all the links of the walk, name-not-utf8, an entry whose name is not valid UTF-8, so that no text names it, and link-path-too-long, a symbolic link whose chain passes, on the way, a path longer than the system takes (4,095 bytes), which the walker cannot walk as the system would; none is ever read, and all three are counted and named with the others in the not-readable-as-code member. It breaks in the same ONE direction as (4), (9) and (10): a document written before this date is still valid here; a document carrying a new value is INVALID against any copy of this schema pinned before it. THE POPULATION OF AFFECTED DOCUMENTS IS EXACTLY THE SCANS OF A TREE THAT HOLDS SUCH AN ENTRY (a clone can carry both). Until this date such a link was resolved by the system however long its chain, and read where it led to a file of the tree, and such a name was handed back to the system as text that named another entry or none (refused as could-not-open, or, where another entry bore that text, that entry read or walked in its place); a scan of any other tree writes the document it wrote before. (12) 2026-11-10: excluded_by_walker[].reason gained git-lfs-pointer, a file that is exactly a Git LFS pointer (its content never checked out), never read and named in the not-readable-as-code member with its own count git_lfs_pointers_not_read; until this date such a pointer was read as code, and its oid line could fire as a credential. A file that starts with a UTF-16 byte-order mark is read, decoded from UTF-16, where it was refused as binary-content; the same member counts it (files_read_from_utf16), and counts the files read with bytes that are not UTF-8 (files_read_with_bytes_not_utf8). A scan of a tree holding none of these writes the document it wrote before.

scan_id.description: Identifier for this scan run, used to tie findings to their evidence log.

bundle.description: The compiled rule bundle these findings came from. Recorded so a result can be reproduced later, once the rules have moved on.

version.description: Bundle version (YYYY.MM.n). Copied verbatim from the bundle manifest's `bundle_version`, and the pattern is the one bundle-manifest.schema.json states for that field: a constraint that holds where the value is written and not where it is read is decorative one hop downstream, which is how `locations[].file` came to say "relative" in prose and accept `/etc/passwd`.

sha256.description: The bundle's content digest: the sha256 of its file list as `sha256sum` writes one (`<sha256>  <name>` per file the manifest lists, sorted by name, newline after each), computed by the CLI from the files it verified at load and never copied from the manifest. A rebuild of the same rules keeps it; any change to a listed file moves it. Written by every run since 2026-10-12; absent from documents written before.

signature.description: What the CLI could say about the bundle manifest's signature. `unsigned`: the manifest carries the explicit unsigned marker or, in a bundle built before 2026-10-12, `null`. `not-verified`: the manifest carries a signature this CLI has no key to verify. Either way the manifest itself is not authenticated: `sha256` says WHICH rules ran, not WHO published them.

profile_digest.description: Digest of the ScanProfile used, so a run can be tied to its inputs without storing the profile itself. Taken over the profile AS READ: where `profile_validation` records a downgraded field, the digest covers the downgraded value and not the file's own bytes.

profile_validation.description: What checking the ScanProfile against `scan-profile.schema.json` found, and what this run did about it. THE CHECK NEVER REFUSES AND NEVER NARROWS: a violating field is treated as unanswered, which is the state in which every rule naming it still runs and carries the open question, and a profile that is not an object of answers is discarded whole, which is the state in which every rule runs. Both are widenings, which is what makes it safe to apply to somebody's declaration without asking first. Emitted only where `--profile` was given, because with no profile there is nothing to check: `profile_digest: null` with this absent is a run that was given no profile, and a digest with this absent is a document written before 2026-09-02.

ran.description: Whether the schema check ran at all. `false` is a disclosure and is never a pass — a machine that cannot load the validator still runs the scan, and what it does not get is silence.

valid.description: Whether the profile matched the schema. Always `false` where `ran` is `false`, because a check that did not run has established nothing.

unavailable_reason.description: Why the check did not run: the validator could not be loaded, the file could not be read as JSON, or the file is not a JSON object. Empty when the check ran, and never empty when it did not.

profile_treated_as.description: What the run did with the profile as a whole. `as-written` covers THREE states and is read with `ran` AND `valid`, never with either alone: the valid profile (`ran: true`, `valid: true`); the one nothing could check, which is used as written and is exactly why `ran: false` is a disclosure rather than a pass; and the one that WAS checked, is invalid, and had nothing that could be downgraded — a missing required field is absent already, so there is no value to replace (`ran: true`, `valid: false`). Corrected 2026-09-02: this said the first two were told apart by `ran`, which does not separate the third from the first.

violations.description: Every violation, in the order the validator reported them. Empty where the profile is valid, and empty where the validator could not be loaded. NOT EMPTY WHERE THE CHECK DID NOT RUN AT ALL: a file that is not JSON, and a file that is not a JSON object, each carry one violation at `/` with `ran: false` — those are the loudest cases the block has, and reading `ran: false` as "nothing to look at" would skip them. Corrected 2026-09-02 after an independent check measured this description contradicting the code that writes it.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the profile, `/` being the profile itself. For a missing required field it is the field the person has to add, not the object it belongs to; for an unknown extra field it is the extra field, not its parent.

expected.description: What `scan-profile.schema.json` requires at that path, in the validator's own words, with the parameter appended for the keywords whose message names nothing on its own.

found.description: The value that was there, as JSON, truncated past 200 characters and marked when it is. THIS IS WHERE THE FILE'S OWN ANSWER SURVIVES: the profile carried in the same document is the profile as read, so a downgraded field reads `null` there, and the rejected value is here beside the path it sat at. One profile per run and one record of what it was, rather than two profiles that can disagree.

treated_as.description: What the run did with it, in a sentence. Never a repair and never a guess: the field becomes unanswered, or — where the whole file is not an object of answers — the profile is treated as absent. A missing required field says that there is nothing to downgrade, because an absent field is already unanswered.

target.description: Root of the scanned tree; file paths below are shown relative to it.

stats.description: Coverage of the run. Needed to tell an empty result apart from a scan that never looked. Every property here counts files, rules or candidates, so each carries `minimum: 0`: a negative counter is not a small error, it is a counter that ran backwards, and until 2026-08-13 `files_scanned: -42` validated.

rules_suppressed_by_precondition.description: Rules that never ran because the ScanProfile put them out of scope. ZERO ON EVERY SCAN FROM 2026-08-27, AND WRITTEN RATHER THAN DROPPED: nothing in a ScanProfile removes a rule from a scan any more, the eight pass-1 documents on disk carry non-zero values here, and a consumer that reads it must keep getting an answer. Its successor is rules_run_on_declared_inapplicable_precondition, which counts the same rules on the other side of the change - they ran.

rules_run_on_unanswered_precondition.description: Rules that RAN although one of their applicability_preconditions names a ScanProfile field this profile does not answer. These are rules that ran, so this is never a subset of rules_suppressed_by_precondition. Before 2026-08-25 an unanswered question was read as an answer of no and the rule was removed from the scan, so this population sat inside that counter and the document said the person had put the rule out of scope when the person had said nothing at all. Owner ruling, 2026-08-25: an unanswered switch must not delete anything.

rules_run_on_declared_inapplicable_preco.description: Rules that RAN although the profile's own answers put them out of scope. Until 2026-08-27 this population WAS rules_suppressed_by_precondition - the same rules, on the other side of the change, when the answer stopped them from reading a line. A separate counter rather than a correction inside that one, because a reader must not have to subtract to get either. A cost figure and never a quality figure: how many rules read the tree on a premise the person denied, not how many of them were right to.

candidates_suppressed_by_guard.description: Candidates a guard_missing pattern removed before adjudication. Listed individually under suppressed_by_guard.

matches_suppressed_by_corroboration.description: Match LINES a detector.also_in_file gate removed before they could become candidates, summed over the decisions listed in suppressed_by_corroboration — the same relationship files_excluded_by_walker has to excluded_by_walker, and asserted as arithmetic by a check. The unit word differs from candidates_suppressed_by_guard above deliberately: both count match lines, and calling them candidates is inaccurate in both places, because a suppressed line never reached the fingerprint collapse and so was never a candidate — forty-seven lines of one file routinely collapse into one. Renaming the older counter is a contract change and was not taken here. Zero on a bundle where no rule declares detector.also_in_file; nine of the 56 rules declare it today.

files_excluded_by_walker.description: Files the walker refused to open, where it enumerated them. Generated trees are skipped without descending and contribute 0 here; excluded_by_walker records them with files: null so that "not counted" is never read as "nothing there".

files_not_read_by_engine.description: Files the ENGINE opened and then read to no rule - the same relationship files_excluded_by_walker has to excluded_by_walker, one layer further in. A subset of files_skipped, which also carries every walker skip and therefore cannot be decomposed by a reader; files_not_read names every one of them.

files_partially_read.description: Files the engine READ with at least one line blanked by the minification ceiling - the length of files_partially_read, which names every one of them and every line it lost. The ceiling did not move (it is still MINIFIED_LINE_LIMIT and still a proxy); from 2026-09-07 it is applied to the LINE rather than to the file, so a file with one 21,277-character line among 2,479 ordinary ones is read, minus that line, instead of being refused whole. NEVER ADDED TO files_not_read_by_engine OR TO files_skipped: those two are files that were not scanned, these were scanned and are inside files_scanned. Written on every scan, zero included, for the reason files_not_read is emitted when empty - a counter present only when something happened cannot be told apart from a producer that stopped writing it.

files_stopped_for_time.description: Files whose read the PER-FILE WALL-CLOCK BUDGET stopped (--file-budget, 60 seconds by default): the rows of files_partially_read that carry a stopped_for_time block, plus the rows of files_not_read whose reason is time-budget. Never a second tally - it is recomputable from the two arrays, both of which are written on every scan. WRITTEN ONLY WHEN IT IS NON-ZERO, WHICH IS WHY ITS MINIMUM IS 1 AND NOT 0, and it is the only counter in this block written that way. Every other counter here is written zero included, because a counter present only when something happened cannot be told apart from a producer that stopped writing it; that argument does not reach this one, because the fact it states is already in the document without it - a reader asks the two always-present arrays and gets an answer, and a producer from before the budget existed gives the same answer, no file was cut short for time, because it had no budget to cut one short with. What writing it unconditionally WOULD cost is the property the budget was approved under: a scan whose files all finish inside the budget writes the document it wrote before the budget existed, byte for byte. A key whose only value on such a run is 0 would end that for every tree to buy nothing. THE DECISION WAS RE-TAKEN ON 2026-09-16 AND KEPT, after independent verification asked for both readings, and the reasoning is written here rather than left to a precedent because the precedent differs in kind: gates_opened_by_scope is written when the BUNDLE declares gate_scope, so for a given bundle its presence is fixed and the same for every tree, while this key's presence depends on the tree AND on how busy the machine was. What decided it is not the precedent but the property: byte identity of a scan that stops nothing is the standing gate of the whole speed-up lane, every step of which is held against it, and this key is the only thing in step 4 that would break that identity on every tree at once. Added 2026-09-16.

files_comment_syntax_unregistered.description: Files the engine read WHOLE and whose COMMENTS it therefore read as CODE, because strip-comments.ts has no comment syntax registered for their extension (syntaxFor answers null; "none" is a different answer and means the format genuinely has no comment form, as .json and .txt do). THE ONLY COUNTER IN THIS BLOCK THAT SIZES FILES READ TOO GENEROUSLY rather than not enough: these files are inside files_scanned and every line of them reached every rule, including the comment lines, so a maintainer's note saying "we do not delete anything" is offered to 117 rules as though the product executed it. NEVER ADDED TO files_not_read_by_engine OR TO files_skipped. Written on every scan, zero included, for the reason files_partially_read is. Reported in coverage_limits; the repair is a row in BY_EXT and is an engine backlog item rather than a scan-time option.

files_comment_form_read_as_code.description: Files the engine read WHOLE whose extension IS registered in strip-comments.ts, but whose language has a comment form the registered mode reads as CODE, and which carry that form where the rules read it (the comment-blanked view). THE CLASS files_comment_syntax_unregistered CANNOT SEE: that counter asks whether any grammar is registered, and a family registration (hash, line-hash, c-like, css) answers yes for a language whose comment grammar is larger than the family's - which is how Ruby's =begin blocks were read as code while it read 0 (architecture review 2026-09-14, A1). The forms are declared in strip-comments.ts COMMENT_FORMS_READ_AS_CODE and named in comment_forms_read_as_code; a file carrying two forms counts once here. A SIZE, NOT A REPAIR: never added to files_comment_syntax_unregistered or any other counter, and not part of coverage_limits. Written on every scan, zero included. Added 2026-10-12.

comment_forms_read_as_code.description: files_comment_form_read_as_code by form: for each comment form declared in strip-comments.ts COMMENT_FORMS_READ_AS_CODE, the files whose comment-blanked view still holds it. Every declared form is a key, zero included, so a form that stopped being counted cannot be told apart from one that found nothing only by reading the code; the key set is the declaration's and is not repeated here. The values are file counts.

manifests_not_usable.description: REFUSALS the CENSUS recorded while reading package.json manifests: one per file that fails JSON.parse (a UTF-8 BOM is enough, and npm itself accepts one), and one per block whose value is a string, a number or an array rather than a name-to-version map. A COUNT OF REFUSALS, NOT OF FILES - one manifest with two malformed blocks counts 2, and since 2026-08-28 there are four blocks it can happen in. THE BLOCK-LEVEL REFUSAL IS PER BLOCK: a manifest whose devDependencies is malformed still contributes every package its dependencies block declares, and it is counted here for the block that was refused - which means a non-zero count here does NOT mean a manifest contributed nothing. A DIFFERENT POPULATION from files_not_read_by_engine and never added to it - those files reached no rule, these reached every rule and were refused by the dependency parse alone. Added 2026-08-28: until then the parse failure was swallowed, so dependency_inventory [] from a manifest the census could not read was indistinguishable from dependency_inventory [] from a tree with no npm manifest, while the inventory's own description told the reader that an empty inventory is a statement about npm manifests - the forbidden state, an absence read as an answer, one level down. Measured over the 3,507 package.json files of the 98-tree corpus: 0 fail JSON.parse and 0 carry a BOM, so it is 0 on every tree read so far. Written on every scan, zero included, for the reason declared_only is: a counter present only when something failed cannot be told apart from a producer that stopped writing it. CensusResult.manifests_not_usable in the reconcile input names the files and says why.

derived_views_built.description: Files for which a rule declaring detector.gate_view, detector.resolve_import_aliases or detector.resolve_local_values asked for a derived view and one was produced. THE NUMBER IS A SUM OVER SEVERAL READINGS AND NAMES NONE OF THEM: both members of detector.gate_view - "yaml-anchors", the document with anchors, aliases and merge keys resolved, and "comments-visible", the file's own text with nothing blanked - are counted here, alongside the alias and local-value probes. Demand-driven: every one of them is attempted only when the declaring rule reaches the point of needing it, which for a gate view means only when that rule's gate would otherwise be shut, so this counts the work the scanned tree actually caused rather than the files that could have caused it. To learn WHICH reading was consulted for a particular suppression, read suppressed_by_corroboration[].cause, and to learn what a rule declared, read its own detector in rules.json.

derived_views_failed.description: Files where a declared derived view could not be produced — malformed YAML, a recursive anchor, a document over the size ceiling, or, from 2026-09-07, a YAML file the minification ceiling reduced (the yaml-anchors view PARSES the document and a blanked line changes the document it would parse, so the view is refused on such a file). APPLICABILITY IS ASKED FIRST: a file this view never had an answer for - anything that is not .yaml or .yml - stays not-applicable and is not counted here, the same order the structural reading uses for no-adapter. Without that order the counter read 731 over fifteen corpus trees where 730 of the files were not YAML. WHICH files this cause can apply to is recoverable from files_partially_read, which is why the cause is not lost by sharing this counter — and the gate fell back to the file's unexpanded text. A fallback can never lose a candidate that was found without the view, because the file's own text is always tested first; it is counted rather than logged for the same reason as suppressed_by_guard, that a degrade nobody can see is a degrade nobody audits.

gates_opened_by_scope.description: (rule, file) corroboration gates that were SHUT on the file's own comment-blanked text and were opened by a wider detector.gate_scope, which is the count of what that field did on this tree. ABSENT WHEN NO RULE IN THE BUNDLE DECLARES A WIDER SCOPE, and present with its true value - zero included - as soon as one does. That is the opposite convention from the counters above it, which any bundle can move and which are therefore written on every scan. A bundle where nothing declares the field cannot move this counter at all, and the proof the mechanism shipped under is that such a scan's document is identical to the one written before the field existed, so its absence states `no rule in this bundle can widen a gate`, its 0 states `one can and none did on this tree`, and the two are different facts rather than a producer that stopped writing a key. A COUNT OF GATE DECISIONS, NOT OF CANDIDATES: one opened gate releases every line that gate held in that file, and each of those lines is an ordinary candidate whose location carries corroborated_from.

joined_views_built.description: ABSENT WHEN NO RULE IN THE BUNDLE DECLARES detector.join_bracketed_constructs, and present with its true value — zero included — as soon as one does. derived_views_built and derived_views_failed above are written on every scan because any bundle can move them; none of these three can move at all for a bundle where nothing declares the view, and the default-unchanged proof the view ships under is that such a scan's document is the one written before the view existed. So absence states "no rule here folds anything" and 0 states "one can and this tree gave it nothing", which are different facts. FILES for which a declaring rule had a joined view built and at least one construct was folded onto its opening line. Counted apart from derived_views_built rather than added to it: that counter already carries the YAML expansions and the two substitution probes together, and a fold is a different reading with a different cost that a reader has to be able to size on its own.

joined_views_not_applicable.description: ABSENT WHEN NO RULE IN THE BUNDLE DECLARES detector.join_bracketed_constructs, and present with its true value — zero included — as soon as one does. derived_views_built and derived_views_failed above are written on every scan because any bundle can move them; none of these three can move at all for a bundle where nothing declares the view, and the default-unchanged proof the view ships under is that such a scan's document is the one written before the view existed. So absence states "no rule here folds anything" and 0 states "one can and this tree gave it nothing", which are different facts. FILES a declaring rule asked a joined view for in which NOTHING could be folded — no line opens a bracketed construct that closes inside the ceilings.

joined_constructs_refused.description: ABSENT WHEN NO RULE IN THE BUNDLE DECLARES detector.join_bracketed_constructs, and present with its true value — zero included — as soon as one does. derived_views_built and derived_views_failed above are written on every scan because any bundle can move them; none of these three can move at all for a bundle where nothing declares the view, and the default-unchanged proof the view ships under is that such a scan's document is the one written before the view existed. So absence states "no rule here folds anything" and 0 states "one can and this tree gave it nothing", which are different facts. CONSTRUCTS a ceiling turned down — one that never closes in its file, one longer than the line ceiling, or one that would fold past the character ceiling (derive.ts JOINED_VIEW_LIMITS). A DIFFERENT POPULATION from the two counters above, which count FILES, and the three must never be added together. Every refusal leaves its opening line to be tested exactly as it is without the view, so a refusal can never remove a candidate; it is counted because a degrade nobody can see is a degrade nobody audits.

joined_outer_duplicates_dropped.description: ABSENT WHEN NO RULE IN THE BUNDLE DECLARES detector.join_bracketed_constructs, and present with its true value — zero included — as soon as one does, on exactly the reasoning the three counters above it are written under. CANDIDATES the nested-duplicate collapse removed. A FOURTH POPULATION beside them and never to be added to them: joined_views_built and joined_views_not_applicable count FILES, joined_constructs_refused counts CONSTRUCTS, and this counts CANDIDATES. A construct written inside another is folded at each opening line, so a cookie literal inside a closure inside a function arrived as three candidates carrying one reading; from 2026-09-07 the enclosing one is not reported when EVERY match clause it fired is also fired by candidates of the same rule lying inside its own fold span. THIS IS THE JOINED VIEW'S ONE SUBTRACTION and that is why it is counted at all, since every other counter here sizes a widening or a degrade: a subtraction nobody can size is a subtraction nobody audits. It is never the only trace of a removal — each collapsed opening line is kept on the report that absorbed it, in locations[].also_opens_at, and the total of those entries across the document is this number. An enclosing candidate that fires a clause NOTHING inside it fires is reported unchanged and is not counted here; nothing without a fold span is ever dropped; no line number moves.

structural_trees_built.description: Files the structural (parse-tree) reading successfully parsed. Demand-driven like the derived views: a file is parsed only when a rule declaring detector.structural_checks reaches it, so a bundle where no rule declares one leaves every structural_* count at zero and loads no grammar at all.

structural_no_adapter.description: Files whose language no adapter reads (.py, .go, .php, .json and most of a normal tree). Counted separately from a parse that found nothing, because "the structural side found nothing here" and "the structural side cannot read this" are different answers and adding them together is how a hole becomes invisible.

structural_grammar_unavailable.description: Files whose grammar could not be loaded in this process — a missing vendored .wasm, or a runtime that would not start. Each falls back to the line-based reading, which has already run, so no candidate is lost; the languages are named once each with their error under structural_grammars_unavailable, while this counts every file that hit one.

structural_parse_failed.description: FILES where the parse or the adapter threw, and nothing else. Falls back to the line-based reading. Counted because a failure nobody counts is a failure nobody notices: the prototype saw zero of these over 34,110 files, which is exactly why an uncounted one would go unnoticed. Until 2026-08-11 this also counted discarded findings, so it mixed two units and the number of failed files could not be read off it; that half is now structural_findings_out_of_range.

structural_skipped_too_large.description: Files the structural reading refused on the size ceiling, which is the walker's own file ceiling rather than a second policy. Falls back to the line-based reading.

structural_skipped_partial_source.description: Files the structural (parse-tree) reading refused because the minification ceiling had blanked a line in them. A parse tree built from text with an emptied line is a tree of a document that does not exist - the line closes no tag it opened and leaves the brace it opened open - so a check reading it would report structure the file does not have, at line numbers that are real. Each such file is read by the line-based patterns only, which is strictly more than it got before 2026-09-07, when the whole file was refused to every rule alike. Counted apart from structural_skipped_too_large because "there is too much of it" and "this is not the document" are different refusals; files_partially_read names the files.

structural_findings_out_of_range.description: FINDINGS discarded because a check emitted a line outside the file it was reading — the engine's backstop on the guarantee that every reported line is a line of the original file. A different event and a different unit from structural_parse_failed: that counts files nothing was read from, this counts findings that were read and not believed, from files that parsed. Never added into the "read by the line-based patterns only" file count.

structural_candidates_added.description: Candidates only the structural reading produced — a location the rule's line patterns did not raise. Reported as product cost, never as a quality signal: layer 2 adjudicates every candidate in the user's own agent and the user pays for it.

structural_candidates_duplicate.description: Structural findings the line-based reading had already produced at the same file and line, emitted once. It earns its place in this list: without it a reader cannot tell "the second eye agreed with the first everywhere" from "the second eye never ran".

structural_candidates_dropped_by_match_w.description: Structural findings a detector.match_without clause removed, tested against the candidate's own reported line. Those clauses are the rule author's measured decisions about lines that are not the construct at all, and a second way of reading the same file is not a second opinion about what the rule targets.

excluded_by_walker.description: What the walker refused to open, aggregated by reason and directory. Emitted for the same reason as suppressed_by_guard: a file the walker never opens can never reach the adjudicating agent, so an exclusion that is wrong is invisible. The non-production exclusion in particular is a single hidden setting deciding the scanning surface of every rule at once, which is what detector.file_globs replaces.

dir.description: Directory the exclusion applies to, relative to the scan root, in the shown form `examples` describes. For a folder whose name is not valid UTF-8 (reason name-not-utf8) it is that folder, which is also its one example, and `files` counts the files below it.

files.description: Files excluded, or null where the tree was not enumerated. `minimum` binds only when the value is a number, so `null` still validates.

examples.description: A few example paths, so the exclusion can be judged without re-running the scan. Every path, with no cap, for the ten reasons about what stood at the path (named-pipe, socket, device, link-to-folder, link-to-nothing, link-to-outside, could-not-open, link-not-followed, name-not-utf8, link-path-too-long). Each path is in the SHOWN FORM, in which a backslash always begins an escape: a backslash of the name is written as two backslashes and a byte that is not valid UTF-8 as a backslash, x and two hex digits, so a path here names exactly one entry; a name with neither is its text. A path the scan read (a candidate's file) is its text and is never in this form; every path here was not read.

coverage_limits.description: WHAT THIS SCAN READ PAST, AND WHAT WOULD OPEN IT - every way this scan fell short of reading the whole tree, each with its count, the option that lifts it where one exists, and the ONE sentence every output prints. Owner decision, 2026-09-10, and the reason it is one model rather than a block about the new read scope alone: a scan falls short in five ways and reporting one of them in its own words, in one output, leaves a reader four silences to discover separately and lets the console, the SARIF and the layer-2 report say different things about the same tree. It is a READING of the fields around it - excluded_by_walker, files_not_read, files_partially_read, stats and rules_without_candidates - and never a second tally, so every number here can be checked against the field beside it. Every member is present whatever its counts say, zero included, because "nothing was held back" and "this scanner does not check" are different facts and an absent member cannot tell them apart. Absent only from a document written before 2026-09-10.

version.description: Versioned with the findings document: a consumer that knows version 1 knows the member ids below and the order they arrive in.

limits.description: The members, in model order: one per read-scope class the bundle declares, then refused-by-rule, not-readable-as-code, rules-not-run, rules-silent.

id.description: read-scope:<class>, refused-by-rule, not-readable-as-code, rules-not-run or rules-silent. Stable, because the SARIF alert's identity across commits is derived from it: a member id that moved would close and re-open an alert on a tree nobody touched.

counts.description: The counts this member states, each under its own name and in its own unit. Counts are never added across members, and the key names say what the unit is (directories, files, lines, rules).

sentence.description: THE ONE WORDING. The console block, the SARIF note-level results and the layer-2 report all print exactly this string and none of them composes its own, so no member can be phrased one way on the console and another way in the Security tab.

lift.description: The option that lifts this limit, or null where nothing does today. null is a statement to the reader that they cannot change it, not a missing value.

read.description: Read-scope members only: whether the run opted into this class with --read. false with counts of 0 is a class that held nothing back in this tree; true is a class the run read.

patterns_set.description: Read-scope members only: the sets of rules/path-exclusions/ this class is composed of, so the reader can see which spellings held a path back.

patterns_source.description: Read-scope members only: the file those sets are declared in. A class is one file of rules/path-exclusions/, because each of those files declares exactly one question in its own header.

rules.description: rules-not-run only, and only where --rules narrowed the run: the rules the run was narrowed to.

files_not_read.description: Every file the engine opened and then handed to no rule, NAMED, with the reason and with the measurement the decision was taken on. The third of this document's three refusal channels and the last one that was silent: excluded_by_walker says what was never opened, this says what was opened and then set aside, and suppressed_by_guard / suppressed_by_corroboration say what matched and was then removed. Present even when empty: an absent key would be indistinguishable from a scanner that does not record. Owner ruling, 2026-08-25: do not remove the skip, report it.

file.description: Path relative to the scan root, exactly as the walker produced it.

reason.description: long-line: NO line of the file is under the minification ceiling, so nothing was left to read once the over-long lines were taken out. This is strictly narrower than it was before 2026-09-07, when the row meant only that the file CONTAINED such a line: a document with one squashed value among 2,478 ordinary lines is not in this array at all any more, it is in files_partially_read and was read minus that line. What is here is what the ceiling exists for - measured over fifteen corpus trees, 398 of the 1,201 files it touched. That ceiling is a PROXY for build output and is reported rather than assumed - a long line is not a bundle, and measured on this workspace's own tree on 2026-09-07, 23 authored files under rules/ exceed it. unreadable: the file could not be read as UTF-8 text when the engine asked for it (removed, permission denied, a race with another process). time-budget: the per-file wall-clock budget (--file-budget, 60 seconds by default) was already spent when the first rule reached the first line, so NO RULE READ A LINE of this file; budget_ms and elapsed_ms carry the measurement it was stopped on. That is the rare half of the budget - the ordinary case is a file the budget stops part-way through, which is in files_partially_read with a stopped_for_time block because lines WERE read. A row here means none were, and a scan run with --file-budget off can never write one. Added 2026-09-16.

longest_line.description: Characters in the file's longest line. Present for long-line.

threshold.description: The ceiling that line exceeded, carried per row so the record is self-describing when the ceiling later moves.

detail.description: What the runtime said, for unreadable.

budget_ms.description: The per-file wall-clock budget in force, in milliseconds. Present for time-budget. At least 1: resolveFileBudgetMs refuses a --file-budget that rounds to 0 ms, so no document can carry a budget that stops every file before its first line (independent verification note F2, 2026-09-16, which measured --file-budget 0.0004 writing budget_ms 0 here and being rejected by evidence-log.schema.json, where the same field is minimum 1). The two schemas describe the same number and now agree on its bound.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this file had already cost when the budget stopped it. Present for time-budget, and always at least budget_ms: the clock is read between lines, so the reading that stops a file is taken after the work that overran it. On this path the overrun is in the file's own read, the comment-blanking pass or the first rule's gate test rather than in a line loop, so the excess is whichever of those was running - see files_partially_read.stopped_for_time.elapsed_ms for the bound the line loop gives.

files_partially_read.description: Every file the engine READ with at least one line blanked by the minification ceiling, NAMED, with each blanked line and the length it held. A DIFFERENT POPULATION FROM files_not_read AND NEVER ADDED TO IT: that array is the files no rule read at all, this is the files every rule read, minus some lines. Both exist for one argument at two units - files_not_read was added on 2026-08-25 because "we did not read this file" and "there was nothing in this file" were the same output, and this is added on 2026-09-07 because the same sentence is true of a line. THE LINE NUMBERS ARE THE FILE'S OWN: a blanked line is emptied in place and never removed, so the count of lines in the file is unchanged, every reported line number in this document still names the line a reader can open, and a blanked line can be a candidate no more than an empty line can. TWO READINGS ARE REFUSED on a file listed here, and it is the only place a reader can learn which files they are: the yaml-anchors gate view and the structural reading both parse the document, and a blanked line changes the document they would parse. Every other reading is line-local and is unaffected. Present even when empty, like files_not_read: "every file was read whole" is a statement about this scan, and an absent key would be indistinguishable from a scanner that does not record. Owner approval 2026-09-07 (engine proposal 2 item 1); the 2026-08-25 ruling - do not remove the skip, report it - keeps all of its substance, because a blanked line still reaches no rule, no quote and no adjudicator. TWO CAUSES SINCE 2026-09-16 AND A ROW SAYS WHICH IT IS BY WHICH BLOCK IT CARRIES: lines is the minification ceiling, stopped_for_time is the per-file wall-clock budget (--file-budget, 60 seconds by default), and a row carries at least one of the two and may carry both. That is why file is now the only required property: a file the budget stopped and the ceiling never touched has no ceiling to name, and writing threshold anyway would state a measurement nobody took.

file.description: Path relative to the scan root, exactly as the walker produced it.

threshold.description: The ceiling these lines exceeded, carried per row so the record is self-describing when the ceiling later moves. Present exactly when lines is.

lines.description: Every line replaced by the empty string, in ascending line order. Never empty and never written empty: a file with no over-long line does not carry this property at all - before 2026-09-16 that meant it was not in this array at all, and since then it can be here for the time budget alone.

line.description: 1-based line number in the file as it is on disk. Unchanged by the blanking, which empties the line in place.

length.description: Characters the line held before it was blanked - the measurement the decision was taken on.

stage.description: Where the census stopped: binary-check, long-line-ceiling, line-split, probe:<kind>, swift-manifests, package-manifest, comment-blanking, imports, collector:<name> or request-construct.

budget_ms.description: The file's time budget, in milliseconds (--file-budget).

elapsed_ms.description: What the census had spent on the file when it read its clock and stopped.

lines_read.description: For a stage that reads line by line: the lines it read before the stop.

lines_total.description: For a stage that reads line by line: the file's lines.

census_stopped_for_time.description: The census's stop on this file. The census is a second pass over every file with its own clock per file; when the file's time budget was spent it stopped reading the file at `stage`, keeping what it had raised. Present only on such a file: a file the census read whole carries no such member.

stopped_for_time.description: The PER-FILE WALL-CLOCK BUDGET stopped this file's read, and the measurement it was stopped on. WHAT THE SHAPE MEANS, because it is not "the file was read down to line N": the engine reads a file RULE BY RULE and each rule reads every line - the outer loop is the rules, the inner loop is the lines (scanFile in engine.ts) - so a stop splits the rules into three groups, and the four counts are what lets a reader reconstruct which is which. Rules 1..rules_completed read the WHOLE file and are in this document exactly as they would be without the budget; rule rules_completed+1 read lines 1..lines_read and stopped before the next line, and every candidate it raised over those lines is KEPT; rules rules_completed+2..rules_total never read this file at all. lines_total - lines_read is what the interrupted rule did not see. NOTHING ALREADY RAISED IS DROPPED, and the one reading that can go the other way is stated rather than left to be found: a guard_missing clause of a rule that did not finish is not evaluated on this file, and a guard DELETES candidates, so a stop can leave a candidate standing elsewhere that a complete read would have removed (0 of the shipped rules declare one). Absent from every scan in which no file exceeded its budget, and from every scan run with --file-budget off.

budget_ms.description: The budget in force for this file, in milliseconds. At least 1, for the reason files_not_read[].budget_ms carries: a budget that rounds to 0 ms is refused before the scan starts.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this file had cost when the clock was read. Always at least budget_ms: the clock is read between lines, so the reading that stops a file is taken after the work that overran it. THE DIFFERENCE IS ONE CLOCK WINDOW OF THE INTERRUPTED RULE, which is not the same as one line, and this sentence said "what one line of one rule cost" until 2026-09-16, when independent verification measured overshoots of up to +74 percent of the budget against it. The window is sized from the per-line cost of the window just measured so that it cannot spend more than a quarter of the budget REMAINING, and it is one line as soon as fewer than four such lines fit in what is left - so a rule whose per-line cost is steady stops within one line of the budget (re-measured at 9, 10, 11 and 12 second budgets: +0.4 to +1.9 percent). What can still overshoot by a whole window is a rule whose per-line cost rises sharply inside one window, which no clock read less often than every line can see coming. Treat this number as a measurement of one run on one machine, never as a bound the tool guarantees.

lines_read.description: Lines of this file the INTERRUPTED RULE read before the stop; the stop is before line lines_read+1. 0 IS A REAL VALUE AND MEANS SOMETHING PRECISE: the clock ran out on the interrupted rule's own first reading of line 1, before that line was read - so with rules_completed above 0 the file WAS read, whole, by every rule before this one, and this row is where it says so. The one combination that cannot appear is 0 with rules_completed 0, which is a file no rule read a line of: that is in files_not_read with reason time-budget.

lines_total.description: Lines the file has. Unchanged by the stop - nothing is removed from the file's own numbering.

rules_completed.description: Rules that had FINISHED WITH this file when the stop came, counted in the bundle's own compiled order: those that read every line of it, AND those that declined it on file_globs or path_without without opening it. The second group is counted deliberately and the wording says so because it used to say "read the whole file", which was exact only while no rule excluded the stopped file by glob. The property this count is for is subtraction: rules_total minus rules_completed is the number of rules that had not finished with the file, i.e. the interrupted rule and every rule below it, and that is the number a reader needs. A rule whose file_globs exclude this file finished with it as surely as one that read it line by line, and counting it anywhere else would make that subtraction wrong. 0 means the stop came inside the first compiled rule's own pass.

rules_total.description: Rules this run compiled - the whole bundle, or the selection --rules narrowed it to. It is the number that would have FINISHED WITH the file had the scan not been stopped, on the same reading as rules_completed: some of them would have declined it rather than read it.

structural_reading_stopped.description: THE STRUCTURAL (PARSE-TREE) READING OF THIS FILE PASSED ITS TIME ALLOWANCE AND WAS ABANDONED. Every rule still read every line of the file; the rules that also read a file as a document (detector.structural_checks) got no parse tree of this one, exactly as when a parse throws, and the file is also counted in stats.structural_parse_failed. Absent on every file whose structural reading finished, was never asked for, or was refused.

allowance_ms.description: The allowance in force for this file, in milliseconds: half its per-file budget, at most 10,000.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds the structural reading had taken when the allowance was read as spent. A measurement of one run on one machine, like stopped_for_time.elapsed_ms.

suppressed_by_guard.description: Candidates removed by a guard, each paired with the guard evidence that removed it. A suppressed candidate never reaches the adjudicating agent, so a guard that is wrong is invisible without this list.

guardLine.description: 0 when the guard matched across a line break and no single line carries it.

suppressed_by_corroboration.description: Every detector.also_in_file gate that shut on a file whose lines the rule's own match patterns did hit — one entry per (rule, file), which is the unit the gate decides in: the gate is evaluated once per file per rule and that one evaluation silences every line below it. The same remedy as suppressed_by_guard, applied to the field that is actually used: no rule has declared detector.guard_missing since the owner removed the mechanism on 2026-07-27 (0 of 56 today), while nine rules declare detector.also_in_file, so until 2026-08-13 this document could describe the suppression that never happens and not the one that, over the 94 pinned corpus trees, happens 11,976 times and removes 28,504 match lines with no trace anywhere. Present even when empty, like suppressed_by_guard: `no gate shut in this tree` is a statement about the tree, and an absent key would be indistinguishable from a scanner that does not record. THE TWO ARRAYS STAY SEPARATE and the reason is the one above, re-checked on 2026-08-27: the schema states no combinators, so a merged array needs either a kind discriminator it cannot express or four required guard fields made optional, which weakens a contract that holds. What was completed instead is THIS record — every removed line is now named in `lines` (by its number only since 2026-09-23, when this document stopped carrying the lines' text — see (7) in the top-level description), with the mechanism that removed it in `cause`, so both arrays name every line they silence and neither is a count standing in for a list. ADDING `cause` AND `lines` TO `required` WAS A BREAKING CHANGE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and it is stated in this file's own top-level description rather than left to be found: a document written before 2026-08-27 fails validation here, and a document written after it fails validation against a schema pinned before it, since this item sets additionalProperties: false. All 20 findings documents frozen under an internal record are in the first class, measured with ajv on 2026-08-27, and none was rewritten. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHAT FIRES: the gate decides exactly what it decided before, and candidates, finding_ids, locations and the SARIF output are byte-for-byte what they were.

rule_id.description: The rule whose gate shut, on the same terms and with the same pattern as candidates[].rule_id.

file.description: Path relative to `target`, on the same terms and with the same pattern as candidates[].locations[].file. A reader opens this path to judge whether the suppression was correct, so it needs the constraint for the same reason a candidate location does.

line.description: First line in this file the gate removed for this rule, 1-indexed as candidates[].locations[].start_line is. Named, never quoted: a reader opens `file` at this line in their own tree.

matches.description: How many lines in this file the gate removed for this rule. At least 1: a gate that shut over a file where nothing matched cost nothing and is not recorded, which is what keeps this array proportional to what was suppressed rather than to the size of the tree. Every one of those lines is named, in `lines`; `line` is the first of them. Until 2026-08-27 only the first was named and this counter was the whole of what the rest amounted to — an internal record recorded that as a known limit and an internal record closes it.

clauses_failed.description: How many detector.also_in_file clauses were tested, every one of which failed. The field is OR-ed in the engine, so a shut gate means the whole disjunction failed and `which clause failed` has exactly one answer: all of them. The clause TEXT is deliberately not copied into each record — it ships whole inside the bundle's rules.json, and a copy in every record would be both large and a fact kept in two places.

cause.description: Which mechanism silenced these lines. `also_in_file` — the clause list was tested against the file's own comment-blanked text and every clause failed, and no derived view was consulted. `also_in_file+gate_view` — the same clause list was ALSO tested against at least one derived view of the file that was actually BUILT (detector.gate_view, derive.ts) and failed there too, so a reader has to account for that second text before concluding the corroboration is absent. WHICH second text it was is the rule's own detector.gate_view in rules.json, and this field does not say: "yaml-anchors" is the .yml/.yaml document re-rendered with anchors, aliases and merge keys resolved, and "comments-visible" is the file's own text with nothing blanked — the reading every gate had before 2026-07-27, which a rule may name for its POSITIVE corroboration only and which nothing may ever offer to the negative guard_missing. A rule may name both, in which case each was tried until one opened the gate. A declared view that could not be produced — malformed YAML, a recursive anchor, a document over the ceiling — was never consulted and does not put a record in the second state; a view that was not applicable to this file, which for "comments-visible" means a file whose raw text equals its comment-blanked text (no comment the stripper recognises), was not built either and likewise does not. The two `+gate_scope` members carry the same warning about the other widening: the rule declared detector.gate_scope directory or project, so the clause list was also weighed against every other file of that scope the rule is allowed to read, and NO FILE IN THE WHOLE SCOPE carried the corroboration — a stronger statement than a shut file-scope gate, and a reader who reads it as the plain `also_in_file` concludes the corroboration may be one file away when the engine has already looked there. Not derivable from anything else in this document: stats.derived_views_built is tree-wide and also counts alias probes, and the rule's own gate_view and gate_scope in rules.json say what was declared rather than what was built or reached.

lines.description: Every line the gate removed in this file for this rule, in ascending file order. ADDED 2026-08-27, and it is what makes this record answer the question it exists to answer. The sibling mechanism suppressed_by_guard, which 0 of 63 rules declare, has recorded every suppressed match individually since 2026-07-27; this is the same completeness applied to the mechanism that actually fires. THE UNIT OF THE RECORD IS UNCHANGED: the gate is evaluated once per (rule, file) and that one evaluation silences every line here, so this is one decision carrying N lines and not N decisions. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHAT FIRES: candidates, finding_ids, locations and the SARIF output are what they were.

line.description: The removed line, 1-indexed as candidates[].locations[].start_line is.

candidates.description: Detector hits awaiting review. Each one is a question for a human or an adjudicator, not a verdict.

finding_id.description: Fingerprint of the candidate. Stable across scans, so a finding can be tracked, suppressed or confirmed over time.

rule_id.description: ID of the rule that raised the candidate. Copied verbatim from the rule's `id`, and the pattern is the one rule.schema.json states for it. Shape only: that the id names a rule the bundle actually ships is a fact about two documents, which no schema can state.

title.description: Title of the rule, copied in so the output reads on its own. The length limit is rule.schema.json's own, for the same reason as `rule_id`'s pattern: the value is copied verbatim, so a limit that binds the author and not the output binds nothing a consumer sees. Raised from 120 to 160 with rule.schema.json's on 2026-09-03, and from 160 to 180 on 2026-09-04.

severity.description: Impact if the candidate turns out to be a real gap.

rule_confidence.description: 0..1 confidence in the detector, carried over from the rule. The range is rule.schema.json's own; before 2026-08-13 the prose said 0..1 and the schema accepted -3.

locations.description: Where the rule matched. A candidate always points at code; findings with no location are not reported.

file.description: Path relative to `target`, as the walker produces it (`path.relative`), so `/` on POSIX and `\` on Windows. Until 2026-08-13 "relative" was prose and nothing enforced it: every location in every document could be replaced by `/etc/passwd` with the schema and its gate both green, and a consumer resolving that path reads a file outside the scan. The pattern rejects a leading separator, a leading drive letter, and any `..` PATH SEGMENT; it deliberately accepts `..` INSIDE a name, because `[[...slug]]` is a Next.js catch-all route and 309 such files sit in this project's own corpus. One legitimate POSIX name is rejected with the attacks and cannot be told apart from them by any pattern: a file at the scan root whose name begins with a single letter and a colon (`a:b.ts`), which is a Windows drive-relative path when the same string is read on Windows. The same name one directory down is accepted.

start_line.description: 1-indexed, as every editor and every line-numbered view of the file is. `0` and `-5` both validated until 2026-08-13.

end_line.description: 1-indexed, and never before `start_line`. Set only where the reading that produced the candidate knows it - today, only the structural one.

line_key.description: The fingerprint of this location's line text (place-key.ts `lineKeyOf`): sha256 of `place-text|` and the line as the matcher read it (trimmed, cut to 300 characters), passed through the printed-text credential rule, every program redaction marker made `[redacted]` and white space folded; the first 16 hex digits. A place's identity across runs is its file and this, so a line that moved is the same place. Holds nothing of a credential.

resolved_from.description: The same-file definitions this location was reached THROUGH. Written only by the local-value reading (`detector.resolve_local_values`), and only where a substitution is what made the line match. `start_line` is the USE site, whose own text does not contain the value the rule matched - `fetch(HOST)` says nothing about `example.com` - so without this a reader is handed a line that does not show the thing the rule says it found. Each entry names the definition's line and never quotes it; the reader opens `definition_line` in `file`. Absent on every location a rule matched directly, which is all of them for every rule that does not declare the field.

name.description: The name as the definition wrote it, sigil included (`HOST`, `$host`, `@endpoint`), so the reader can search for it.

definition_line.description: The line that bound the name, 1-indexed, as `start_line` is. In the SAME file as `file`, always: this reading never crosses a file boundary. It may be before or after `start_line`.

corroborated_from.description: The OTHER FILE whose own text opened this candidate's corroboration gate. Written only where the rule declared a wider detector.gate_scope AND its gate was shut on this file's own text, so the candidate exists because a fact the rule requires is written elsewhere in the scope; absent on every location whose own file carried the corroboration, which is all of them for every rule that does not declare the field. It exists for the reason resolved_from does: a reader who cannot see the corroboration cannot check the reading, and a candidate nobody can check is worse than one that was never raised. ONE file and not a list — the gate is a disjunction that stops at the first clause that matches, so there is exactly one file the engine can name, the first in walk order whose comment-blanked text satisfied a clause. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the two files belong to the same code path. It establishes that the fact is written somewhere in the declared scope, which is a weaker statement than the file scope's.

file.description: Path relative to `target`, on the same terms and with the same pattern as this location's own `file`, and never equal to it: at file scope there is no other file to name and this object is not written. A reader opens this path to check the corroboration, so it needs the constraint for the same reason a candidate location does.

line.description: The line of that file the clause's match STARTS on, 1-indexed as start_line is. THE MINIMUM IS 1 FROM 2026-09-06 AND WAS 0 BEFORE IT. A gate clause is tested against the whole comment-blanked file text, so it may match across a line break; the engine used to look for the first single line that matched the clause on its own and wrote 0, with the text `(matched across lines)`, when no line did. That was half of the corroboration records the first rule opt-in produced on real trees, and a record with no line to open does not meet the reason this object exists — a reader who cannot see the corroboration cannot check the reading. The engine now takes the match on the whole text and reports the line its first character is on, which always exists, so 0 can no longer be written and the schema no longer permits it. The remainder of a multi-line construct is on the lines below the one named; no record can name two lines. suppressed_by_guard.guardLine still carries the older reading and keeps its minimum of 0. WHERE A DERIVED VIEW OPENED THE GATE there is no record at all rather than a record with no line: gate_view builds a string with its own line structure that is not the file's, so the engine registers a corroborator only where the file's OWN text satisfied a clause (a view can still open that file's own gate, and then the file raises no candidate needing corroboration).

scope.description: The scope the rule declared, so a reader knows how far the engine was allowed to look before it found this file: `directory` means the same immediate parent directory as this location's own file, `project` means anywhere in the scan. `file` cannot appear — at file scope no other file is consulted and no such record is written.

corroborated_in_project.description: WHETHER THE DECLARED SCOPE CARRIES THIS RULE'S CORROBORATOR VOCABULARY ANYWHERE — a fact layer 1 computed about the WHOLE SCAN, handed to the adjudicating seat as a named premise instead of being used to delete anything. Written only on locations whose fired clauses are all named by the rule's detector.gate_applies_to, and only for a rule whose detector.gate_mode is `annotate`; absent from every location of every rule that declares no subject, which is every rule but the ones that opt in. BOTH VALUES ARE WRITTEN, and `false` is the point of the field: it says the scan found none of the rule's purpose-built vocabulary anywhere in the scope, which is a strong reason for a reader to dismiss the candidate — a reason, never a removal, because a null result is not evidence that nothing is there and subtraction is the only operation that can create a miss. `true` establishes that the vocabulary exists somewhere in the scope and NOTHING MORE: not that the two sites are on one code path, and not that the candidate is real. At project scope the answer is one fact per scan, identical on every location that carries it, which is why it is not part of the candidate's kind key and cannot split a census bin.

corroborated_in_project_from.description: WHERE that corroboration is — written only beside `corroborated_in_project: true`, and absent beside `false`, because a fact that was not found has no line to open. The same shape as corroborated_from and NOT the same claim, which is why it is a separate field rather than a reuse: corroborated_from names the other file that opened a gate SHUT on this location's own file, and can never be this location's own file; this record names the first file in walk order whose own text carries the vocabulary, WHICH MAY BE THIS LOCATION'S OWN FILE, because nothing here was gated. One file and not a list, for the reason corroborated_from gives: the clause list is a disjunction that stops at the first clause that matches. At project scope there is exactly one such record per rule per scan, so every annotated location of one scan names the same file and line.

file.description: Path relative to `target`, on the same terms and with the same pattern as this location's own `file`. Unlike corroborated_from.file it MAY equal this location's own file: no gate was shut, so a file that both fires the subject clause and carries the vocabulary is an ordinary corroborator for its whole scope.

line.description: The line of that file the clause's match STARTS on, 1-indexed as start_line is, and never 0 — the engine takes the match on the whole comment-blanked file text and reports the line its first character is on, which always exists. Written by the same registration corroborated_from is written by, so the reading is the same reading; see that field for the 2026-09-06 repair this minimum records.

scope.description: The scope the rule declared, so a reader knows how far the engine was allowed to look: `directory` means the same immediate parent directory as this location's own file, `project` means anywhere in the scan. `file` cannot appear — a rule that names a subject may not declare it (tools/build-bundle.mjs refuses the combination), because a per-file corroboration is the gate this mechanism exists not to be.

joined_from.description: The span of THIS FILE that was folded onto one string to match here. Written only by the joined-construct reading (detector.join_bracketed_constructs), and only where the fold is what made the line match; absent on every location a rule matched on one physical line, which is all of them for every rule that does not declare the field. NOT OPTIONAL WHERE THE FOLD RAISED THE CANDIDATE, and for the reason resolved_from is not: the reported line is where the construct OPENS and its own text does not carry what the rule matched — a cookie literal is reported at `http.SetCookie(writer, &http.Cookie{` and the attributes it never sets are absent four lines below that. A reader handed the opening line alone is reading half a sentence, and a candidate nobody can check is worse than one that was never raised.

start_line.description: The line the construct opens on, 1-indexed. ALWAYS EQUAL TO THIS LOCATION'S OWN start_line: the fold is a second string at the opening line's own index and the candidate is reported there, so this repeats the line rather than naming a new one, and the pair is what makes the span readable without arithmetic.

end_line.description: The line the construct closes on, 1-indexed, and always GREATER than start_line: a construct that opens and closes on one physical line is not folded at all, because there is nothing to join.

also_opens_at.description: Opening lines of the ENCLOSING constructs that were collapsed into this location, ascending. A construct written inside another is folded at each opening line (detector.join_bracketed_constructs), so one cookie literal inside a closure inside a function arrived as three candidates carrying one reading. From 2026-09-07 the enclosing candidate is not reported when EVERY match clause it fired is also fired by candidates of the same rule lying inside its own fold span, and its opening line is recorded here, on the FIRST surviving report, in file order, that lies inside it — one pointer per removal, never one per surviving report, so the entries across a document can be counted. A POINTER, NOT A SECOND LOCATION: the construct that opens at each line named here is still in the file and the reader can open it; what is no longer reported is a candidate carrying nothing this one does not already carry, which is why the line is kept rather than the candidate. AN ENCLOSING CANDIDATE THAT READS SOMETHING ITS CONTENTS DO NOT IS REPORTED UNCHANGED and appears in no such array — a clause requiring a cookie-family word ON THE LINE is satisfied at the enclosing construct, whose opening line carries the word, and not inside it, so that reading exists nowhere else. ON THE LOCATION AND NOT INSIDE joined_from, because the report that absorbs an enclosing fold is frequently not fold-derived at all — an ordinary matched line inside the span — and such a location has no joined_from to hang it on. Absent on every location that absorbed nothing, which is all of them for every rule that does not declare the view; every entry across a document stands for exactly one removed candidate, so their total is stats.joined_outer_duplicates_dropped.

clause.description: WHICH CLAUSE OF THE RULE FIRED ON THIS LINE - the 1-indexed position of the detector clause in the rule's own order, or several joined by `,` (`"16"`, `"1,3"`), which is the numbering a rule author uses when they write "clause (13)". Present on every location of a document written with the kind census on (`--kind-census on`, the default) and on none of a document written with it off.
